preserved_verbatim.S1_opening: Parallel to advances in reanalysis data, machine learning has gained prominence in precipitation forecasting.
preserved_verbatim.Rahman: \citet{rahman2022rainfall} developed a fusion-based system for smart-city rainfall prediction that combines multiple classifiers with fuzzy logic, reporting improvements in prediction accuracy in their study.
preserved_verbatim.deep_learning_transition: With the development of deep learning, more sophisticated spatiotemporal architectures have been explored.
preserved_verbatim.TRU_NET_four_sentences: \citet{adewoyin2021tru} proposed TRU-NET, which incorporates attention mechanisms and ERA5 inputs to produce high-resolution rainfall predictions over the UK. Their model outperformed U-Net baselines and produced competitive results against dynamical forecasts. In their UK daily-rainfall evaluation, the TRU-NET CC variant underpredicted observed amounts above 20~mm\,day$^{-1}$ more than IFS. This daily-scale comparison does not establish the behaviour of the models evaluated here for Dublin regional-mean hourly precipitation.
preserved_verbatim.Singh: At the global scale, \citet{singh2021deep} trained a residual U-Net on reanalysis data in a cubed-sphere framework and reported improved correlation skill over an operational numerical weather prediction system, while also emphasizing the need for hybrid integration and probabilistic evaluation.
preserved_verbatim.Miller: \citet{miller2021analysis} examined short-term and seasonal rainfall forecasts in Kenya and found substantial regional differences in forecasting skill, highlighting the importance of localized validation.
preserved_verbatim.closing: These studies demonstrate the potential of machine learning and deep learning for precipitation forecasting, while also showing that aggregate performance may not fully represent model behaviour under different rainfall conditions.

removed.old_Latif_sentence: \citet{latif2023assessing} reviewed rainfall prediction models and concluded that machine learning methods, particularly recurrent neural networks such as LSTMs, generally outperform traditional statistical approaches, although challenges related to robustness and interpretability remain.

added.new_Latif_sentence: More recently, \citet{latif2023assessing} compared statistical, machine-learning and deep-learning approaches to rainfall prediction and concluded that machine learning performed well across climates and timescales, with LSTM models among the most effective.
